paragraphs: Attention can connect tokens according to their positions or according to their meanings. This paper studies how a learning system can switch between those mechanisms as it receives more training data. It tackles that question through a mathematically solvable attention model, providing a theoretical account of a change in learned behavior.

The model consists of a nonlinear self-attention layer whose query and key matrices share parameters and have low rank. In a limit where data dimensionality and the number of training examples grow together, the authors derive a precise, closed-form description of the lowest achievable empirical loss. The corresponding solution can use either positional or semantic attention.

As the amount of training data increases, the analysis identifies a phase transition from the positional solution to the semantic one. With sufficient data, semantic attention also lets the model outperform a linear positional baseline. These conclusions concern the specified model and asymptotic setting: they explain how an apparently qualitative capability change can arise in that setting.
neurips-2024-a-phase-transition-between-.tldr: A solvable attention model reveals a data-dependent transition from positional to semantic learning.

paragraphs: AUC measures how well a binary classifier ranks positive examples above negative ones, making it useful when the classes are imbalanced. Methods that maximize it commonly assume training and test examples follow the same distribution. This paper considers a particular departure from that assumption: positive examples can change, while the distribution of examples within the negative class stays fixed.

Under this positive distribution shift, the authors derive an expression for test-distribution AUC using three ingredients: the positive training density, the overall training density, and the overall test density. This connects the desired test-time ranking objective to information available without collecting labeled test examples.

The resulting method uses labeled positives and unlabeled examples from training, together with unlabeled examples from the test distribution. Only the training positives require labels. The authors describe the objective as simple to implement and demonstrate effectiveness on four real-world datasets. Its significance is that adaptation targets test AUC directly under the stated shift assumption, rather than treating training AUC as an unchanged proxy.
neurips-2024-auc-maximization-under-posi.tldr: The paper derives an AUC objective that adapts to changing positive examples using labeled training positives and unlabeled training and test data.

paragraphs: BIOSCAN-5M brings together information about more than five million insect specimens to support biodiversity research. Alongside images, it includes taxonomic labels, DNA barcode sequences, assigned barcode index numbers, geographic information, and specimen sizes. This gives researchers several connected views of the same biological specimens instead of relying entirely on visual appearance.

The paper introduces three benchmark experiments. The first trains a masked language model on DNA barcode sequences and examines how this large reference collection affects classification at the species and genus levels. The second investigates whether representations learned through self-supervision support meaningful clustering in a zero-shot transfer task involving images and DNA barcodes.

The third experiment uses contrastive learning to connect DNA, images, and taxonomy within a shared representation space. That space supports taxonomic classification from multiple kinds of information. Together, the dataset and tasks provide a way to investigate how these modalities contribute to classification and clustering, and whether their learned representations capture biologically useful groupings.
neurips-2024-bioscan-5m-a-multimodal-dat.tldr: BIOSCAN-5M pairs information from over five million insects with benchmarks connecting images, DNA barcodes, and taxonomy.

paragraphs: Finetuning a pretrained model still requires selecting examples worth paying to annotate. Active finetuning addresses this choice under a limited labeling budget. This paper argues that existing approaches either introduce bias when selecting batches or emphasize overall data coverage while overlooking examples that help define local decision boundaries.

BiLAF combines two selection stages. It first chooses core samples to capture global diversity, then chooses boundary samples where local decisions are uncertain. Before obtaining ground-truth labels, it identifies estimated class centers, applies a denoising procedure, and repeatedly evaluates candidate boundary examples using a designed selection metric. These internal iterations produce a single selection for annotation.

The approach therefore balances two different reasons an example might be useful: representing the broader dataset and clarifying where neighboring classes separate. Experiments provide both qualitative and quantitative evidence, with BiLAF consistently outperforming the evaluated baselines. The stated findings support incorporating local boundary information alongside global diversity when deciding which samples to label for finetuning.
neurips-2024-boundary-matters-a-bi-level.tldr: BiLAF selects finetuning examples by combining broad data coverage with uncertainty near local decision boundaries.

paragraphs: Causal relationships can differ across a system's operating conditions, but those conditions may themselves depend on variables inside the system. For example, precipitation influences soil moisture regimes. This paper studies causal discovery when context is endogenous in this way, so identifying relationships within a context must account for how that context arises.

The proposed method adaptively combines conditional-independence tests on pooled data with tests on data from individual contexts. Pooled tests infer dependencies among system variables, including the context variable, to avoid introducing selection bias. Context-specific tests then provide information about causal relationships within particular operating conditions.

The authors develop a theoretical framework connecting this testing strategy to structural causal models. They give sufficient assumptions under which the algorithm is sound and its outputs admit a causal interpretation. A simulation study shows behavior consistent with the theory while also informing discussion of limitations and possible extensions. The contribution is a structured way to seek context-specific causal explanations when contexts are generated within the system.
neurips-2024-causal-discovery-with-endog.tldr: An adaptive testing method discovers context-specific causal graphs while accounting for contexts influenced by the system itself.

paragraphs: Synthetic face images can partly reduce privacy-related legal risks in developing face recognition systems. However, models trained on generated faces often perform worse because the images do not provide sufficiently useful distinctions between identities. This paper investigates which properties of synthetic training examples contribute to effective recognition.

The authors identify similarity to an identity center as an important factor. Their findings indicate that examples with a certain degree of resemblance to that center can be especially useful for training. CemiFace turns this observation into a diffusion-based generation method that produces faces at different similarity levels relative to each subject's center.

This control lets the generated dataset include examples chosen for their discriminative usefulness. Experiments show that a modest degree of similarity can yield recognition performance competitive with previous generation methods. The result supports treating distance from an identity center as a meaningful design choice for synthetic datasets, with the reported benefit tied to the similarity levels used in training.
neurips-2024-cemiface-center-based-semi-.tldr: CemiFace controls synthetic faces' similarity to identity centers to generate useful training examples for face recognition.

paragraphs: Language-model training commonly concatenates documents and cuts the result into fixed-length sequences. When attention between documents is masked, a long chunk can contain much shorter effective attention spans. The paper argues that paying a fixed attention cost for these chunks wastes computation, especially because attention becomes expensive as sequence length grows.

Dataset decomposition instead groups sequences into buckets by length, with each sequence drawn from one document. Training samples across these buckets using a curriculum while varying both sequence length and batch size. This makes computational cost track actual document lengths and makes the distribution of training lengths an explicit part of the training procedure.

The authors train a one-billion-parameter model with an 8k context at the same cost as a baseline model with a 2k context. On a web-scale corpus, they report improved standard language and long-context evaluations, reaching target accuracy with up to six times faster training. The findings show that sequence packaging and curriculum can affect both efficiency and learned performance.
neurips-2024-dataset-decomposition-faste.tldr: Grouping document sequences by length and varying the training curriculum improves language-model efficiency and reported evaluation performance.

paragraphs: Scientific design often seeks new candidates with improved properties despite having limited training data. Conventional guided generation uses both a generator and a separate surrogate model to evaluate or guide candidates. PropEn proposes obtaining guidance from relationships among existing examples, avoiding the need to train a discriminator.

The method matches each sample with a similar sample that has a better value of the desired property. These matches expand the training data and encode a direction of improvement. An encoder-decoder learns from the matched pairs, producing a framework intended to work across domains. The authors show that this training approximates the property's gradient while remaining within the data distribution.

Evaluations cover toy problems, therapeutic protein design, and airfoil optimization, with advantages over common baselines. Protein design results also receive wet-lab validation, supporting the approach's competitiveness and effectiveness in that application. The central contribution is to make the training pairs themselves carry optimization guidance, connecting nearby examples to useful changes in the target property.
neurips-2024-implicitly-guided-design-wi.tldr: PropEn learns property improvements from matched examples, enabling guided scientific design without a separately trained discriminator.

paragraphs: Studying increasingly large transformers can reveal how their training behavior depends on model scale. This paper focuses on limits that preserve feature learning: attention layers must remain able to change during training. The central question is which parameterizations produce a mathematically well-defined large-model limit while retaining that ability.

The authors identify suitable parameterizations and analyze several ways to make a transformer infinite. These include increasing the number of attention heads, increasing key and query dimensionality, and increasing depth. Using dynamical mean field theory, they show that the resulting statistical descriptions depend on both the chosen limit and the scaling of attention layers.

Numerical results provide evidence that finite models converge toward the analyzed limits. The limits also maintain appropriately scaled updates for both SGD and Adam. The work therefore supplies a framework for understanding transformer training at large scale while preserving changing attention features, and explains why different routes to larger models need not share one statistical description.
neurips-2024-infinite-limits-of-multi-he.tldr: The paper characterizes large-transformer limits that preserve attention learning and shows how different scaling choices change training dynamics.

paragraphs: Generating executable programs helps language models solve many symbolic tasks, but some reasoning does not translate easily into fully specified code. Commonsense judgments, moral decisions, and sarcasm understanding are examples considered here. COGEX extends program-based reasoning to such tasks through programs whose execution can draw on a language model's knowledge.

The system trains models to produce Python-like pseudo-programs with some leaf function calls left undefined. It then teaches them to emulate execution, including those undefined calls. The program supplies an explicit structure for the reasoning, while the model fills in operations that were not given executable implementations.

To adapt to a task, COGEX searches candidate programs for a single program that performs best across the dataset when pseudo-executed. The authors report large improvements over standard in-context learning on both algorithmic and softer reasoning tasks. These findings support extending code synthesis beyond problems with fully specified symbolic operations, using learned execution to connect program structure with less formal judgments.
neurips-2024-learning-to-reason-via-prog.tldr: COGEX combines pseudo-program generation, learned execution, and program search to improve algorithmic and less formal reasoning.

paragraphs: Medical recordings such as EEG and ECG contain signals across multiple channels and time scales. Medformer is a transformer designed to use those characteristics for classification. The paper positions it alongside approaches based on handcrafted biomarkers and convolutional networks, addressing the comparatively limited exploration of transformers for these data.

Its design has three connected parts. Cross-channel patching captures relationships between channels. Multi-granularity embeddings represent patterns at different scales. A two-stage attention mechanism then learns relationships within each granularity and across granularities. Together, these components let the model combine information about where signals occur across channels with how they develop over different temporal spans.

The authors evaluate Medformer on five public datasets under both subject-dependent and more challenging subject-independent setups. Against ten baselines, it obtains the highest average ranking across the datasets on all six evaluation metrics. These classification results support the usefulness of the architecture for the studied medical time-series tasks, including applications involving myocardial infarction, Alzheimer's disease, and Parkinson's disease.
neurips-2024-medformer-a-multi-granulari.tldr: Medformer combines cross-channel information and multiple temporal scales to improve classification of medical time series.

paragraphs: Sequences of location check-ins contain clues about why people visit places and how they prefer to travel. The paper argues that existing models do not adequately capture these semantic aspects of mobility data. Mobility-LLM adapts a language model to analyze check-in sequences across multiple tasks by making those aspects more accessible to it.

Because a language model cannot directly interpret check-ins, the framework reprograms the sequences into a form it can use. A visiting intention memory network captures intentions associated with individual records. A shared pool of travel-preference prompts guides the model's interpretation of users' broader preferences. These components connect individual visits and travel preferences to the model's semantic processing.

Experiments span four benchmark datasets and three downstream tasks. The authors report significant improvements over existing models, supporting the effectiveness of their approach in the evaluated location-based service settings. The contribution is a structured way to bring language-model capabilities to mobility records while explicitly representing the intentions and preferences those records may reflect.
neurips-2024-mobility-llm-learning-visit.tldr: Mobility-LLM adapts check-in sequences for language models using visiting-intention memory and travel-preference prompts.

paragraphs: Diffusion models can require many sampling steps to generate an image. This paper develops a distillation method that transfers a many-step model into a model using only a few steps. Its focus is on preserving useful information about the clean data throughout the shortened sampling trajectory.

The training procedure matches conditional expectations of clean data given noisy data at points along that trajectory. In plain terms, it aligns the expected clean output associated with a noisy input. The authors interpret this as moment matching and extend recently proposed single-step approaches to a multistep setting, allowing the distilled model several opportunities to refine its output.

Using up to eight sampling steps, the resulting models outperform both their single-step versions and their many-step teachers in the reported ImageNet results, achieving a new state of the art. A large text-to-image experiment also shows promising fast, high-resolution generation directly in image space. That demonstration uses neither autoencoders nor upsamplers, illustrating another setting where the shortened process can be useful.
neurips-2024-multistep-distillation-of-d.tldr: Moment-matching distillation produces few-step diffusion models that outperform their teachers in the reported ImageNet experiments.

paragraphs: NaRCan represents a video using canonical images designed to look natural and support subsequent editing. The challenge is to connect this representation to frames containing motion and deformation while keeping the representative images visually suitable for editing. The framework combines a model of video deformation with a diffusion prior that guides image appearance.

Global motion is modeled with a homography, while multilayer perceptrons capture local deformations left over after that global transformation. This division helps the model represent complex video dynamics. The diffusion prior is introduced early in training so that natural appearance influences how the canonical images are formed.

The framework also incorporates low-rank adaptation and schedules changes to noise and diffusion-prior updates. The authors report a fourteenfold acceleration of training from these techniques. Across the evaluated video-editing tasks, NaRCan outperforms existing approaches and produces coherent, high-quality edited sequences. The findings support combining motion modeling and appearance guidance to obtain canonical representations that are useful for downstream video editing.
neurips-2024-narcan-natural-refined-cano.tldr: NaRCan combines motion modeling and diffusion guidance to create natural canonical images for coherent video editing.

paragraphs: A language model's knowledge cutoff can leave it unfamiliar with newly emerging terms. Existing benchmarks may conceal that weakness when their content is old or restricted to a few fields. NewTerm is designed to evaluate new terminology through a benchmark that can be updated as language and information change.

The authors develop a highly automated construction process intended to maintain benchmark quality with little human effort. They construct annual editions for terms from 2022 and 2023 and state plans for continued yearly updates. This makes the benchmark's refresh process part of the contribution, alongside the evaluation material itself.

Across the tested language models, new terms cause a performance reduction exceeding twenty percent. Updating a model's knowledge cutoff covers some new terminology, but the experiments find that this does not extend to more distant new terms. The paper also examines which term types are difficult and why. These results distinguish acquiring newer knowledge from generalizing successfully to terminology beyond that knowledge.
neurips-2024-newterm-benchmarking-real-t.tldr: NewTerm provides an annually updateable benchmark showing substantial language-model performance drops on newly emerging terms.

paragraphs: Language models can produce fluent explanations while still making arithmetic mistakes. Generating code for calculations can improve accuracy, but the paper identifies speed and security costs in that approach. OccamLLM connects a language model to a symbolic arithmetic architecture, aiming to perform exact calculations within a single autoregressive step.

The language model's hidden states control the symbolic component that carries out arithmetic. The implementation, OccamLlama, combines Llama 3 with OccamNet. This gives the model an arithmetic mechanism whose operations are explicit, supporting the framework's stated goals of faster, more secure, and more interpretable calculation.

OccamLlama achieves one hundred percent accuracy in the reported tests of individual operations, including basic arithmetic, trigonometric functions, logarithms, exponentials, and square roots. It outperforms GPT-4o with and without a code interpreter on those tests and on average across the evaluated mathematical problem-solving benchmarks. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of symbolic integration for the tested arithmetic tasks, including comparisons with a much larger language model.
neurips-2024-occamllm-fast-and-exact-lan.tldr: OccamLLM uses language-model hidden states to control symbolic arithmetic, enabling exact calculations in a single autoregressive step.

paragraphs: Neural tangent kernel theory connects very wide neural networks to kernel regression. Many analyses simplify this connection by using mirrored architectures and initialization so that the initial network output is exactly zero. This paper asks what changes when ordinary random initialization instead produces a nonzero random function.

The authors first prove that gradient-flow training dynamics converge uniformly to those of the corresponding kernel regression problem with a Gaussian-process initial function. They then characterize that function's regularity in interpolation spaces associated with the neural tangent kernel. Almost surely, membership holds below the threshold 3/(d+1) and fails at or above it.

The resulting generalization-error lower bound is of order n raised to −3/(d+3), where n is sample size and d is data dimension. As dimension grows, this bound reflects the curse of dimensionality. The result shows why initialization matters to the theory's account of generalization and supports the authors' qualified conclusion that NTK theory may not explain neural networks' superior empirical performance.
neurips-2024-on-the-impacts-of-the-rando.tldr: Accounting for ordinary random initialization yields an NTK generalization lower bound that retains the curse of dimensionality.

paragraphs: A multimodal model trained with every input type available can struggle when one is missing. Existing distillation methods often try to make the incomplete input's representation match its complete counterpart precisely. This paper argues that missing information makes such exact alignment too restrictive and can encourage reliance on misleading features.

Probabilistic Conformal Distillation represents an incomplete input through a probability distribution in the complete-input feature space. The aim is to learn the range of mapped representations implied by the missing information. Its construction addresses probability extrema at complete-input feature points and geometric consistency between the modeled distributions and their peak points.

This changes the learning target from a single forced match to a distribution that acknowledges ambiguity. Experiments across benchmark datasets show better performance than the compared state-of-the-art methods. The findings support treating uncertainty about absent modalities as part of representation learning, particularly when the available input cannot uniquely determine the representation that all modalities together would have produced.
neurips-2024-probabilistic-conformal-dis.tldr: PCD improves missing-modality robustness by learning distributions over complete-input representations instead of forcing exact feature matches.

paragraphs: Protein function depends closely on three-dimensional structure, yet many protein language models use sequence information without incorporating structure. ProSST combines both within a transformer. Its main design problem is converting spatial information into a representation that can interact effectively with the sequence of protein residues.

The model first breaks structure into local descriptions associated with individual residues and embeds those descriptions as vectors. A pretrained clustering model converts the vectors into discrete structure tokens. Disentangled attention then explicitly learns relationships between residue tokens and structure tokens, allowing the two representations to inform one another.

ProSST is pretrained on millions of protein structures with a masked language-modeling objective, learning contextual representations by recovering masked information. Evaluation covers zero-shot prediction of mutation effects and several supervised downstream tasks. The authors report state-of-the-art performance among the compared baselines. These findings support the combination of discrete structural representations and explicit sequence-structure interaction as an effective approach to the evaluated protein prediction problems.
neurips-2024-prosst-protein-language-mod.tldr: ProSST combines protein sequences with discrete structure tokens and learns their interactions to improve protein prediction tasks.

paragraphs: Reconstructing an image from a small number of noisy measurements can leave many plausible solutions. A learned image prior helps constrain that uncertainty, while a known forward model describes how an image produces measurements. This paper develops a framework that combines unconditional diffusion priors with general forward models, including nonlinear ones.

Diffusion Plug-and-Play alternates between two samplers. One uses only the measurement likelihood to encourage consistency with observations. The other uses only the image prior's score functions to perform diffusion denoising. The authors establish that denoising with white Gaussian noise can be handled rigorously using either stochastic or deterministic diffusion samplers with the same scores trained for generation.

The framework comes with both asymptotic and non-asymptotic performance guarantees. Numerical experiments illustrate its promise on linear and nonlinear reconstruction tasks. Its central contribution is a theoretically supported separation of measurement consistency and learned image structure, allowing the prior and the sensing model to participate through distinct sampling operations.
neurips-2024-provably-robust-score-based.tldr: DPnP alternates measurement-consistency and diffusion-denoising samplers to reconstruct images with theoretical performance guarantees.

paragraphs: Facility location asks where to place a shared facility based on people's reported locations. Strategic participants may misreport to move the facility closer to themselves. A truthful mechanism must prevent them from benefiting through such misrepresentation, while still choosing a location with a good aggregate distance cost.

Earlier learning-augmented work studied deterministic mechanisms supplied with a prediction of the optimal facility location. This paper broadens the question by examining randomized mechanisms and different kinds of predictions. It studies both locations on a line and locations in Euclidean space, asking how prediction information and randomization affect achievable performance under truthfulness.

The results give upper and lower bounds on approximation of the optimal egalitarian social cost, the objective concerned with the worst-served participant. Upper bounds describe performance that mechanisms can achieve, while lower bounds establish restrictions on what is possible. Together, they clarify the scope for prediction-assisted facility placement when strategic incentives remain a requirement, across the geometries and prediction settings considered.
neurips-2024-randomized-strategic-facili.tldr: The paper bounds how well truthful facility-location mechanisms can perform when using randomization and different types of predictions.

paragraphs: Efficient recurrent models have renewed appeal because transformer inference can be costly. This paper compares the architectures through the model sizes needed to represent particular computations. Its results show that the advantage depends on the task and, for transformers, the number of layers.

For index lookup, a one-layer transformer needs only logarithmic width, while a recurrent model requires a linearly sized hidden state. The direction reverses for bounded Dyck-language recognition: constant-size recurrent models suffice, whereas one-layer transformers need linear size. Two-layer transformers of logarithmic size can also perform string equality, disjointness, and nearest-neighbor computations, with linear-size requirements for the comparison architectures specified in the paper.

The constructions use many nearly orthogonal vectors packed into logarithmic-dimensional space. Lower bounds come from communication-complexity reductions, which establish size requirements rather than merely documenting training failures. Experiments on practical sequence lengths complement the theory. Together, the findings connect architectural choice and transformer depth to the memory and interaction requirements of specific tasks.
neurips-2024-separations-in-the-represen.tldr: Theoretical size separations show that transformers and recurrent models have different task-dependent representational advantages.

paragraphs: A pathology image can contain both healthy and cancerous tissue, while its text description gives only a broad slide-level label. Such summaries provide little detail about individual regions. STimage-1K4M addresses this mismatch by pairing small tissue-image tiles with gene-expression information associated with their spatial locations.

The dataset contains 1,149 images derived from spatial transcriptomics, which records gene expression at individual spots within a tissue image. The images are divided into smaller tiles, each paired with a gene-expression vector containing between 15,000 and 30,000 dimensions. Altogether, the resource provides 4,293,195 image-tile and gene-expression pairs.

These pairings connect local tissue appearance to a much richer molecular description than a single high-level text label supplies. The contribution is the dataset and its fine spatial granularity, creating opportunities to study relationships between visual and genomic features. The authors present it as a foundation for further multimodal analysis and computational-pathology applications that need information about specific regions within larger tissue images.
neurips-2024-stimage-1k4m-a-histopatholo.tldr: STimage-1K4M provides over four million tissue-image tiles paired with spatially matched gene-expression measurements.

paragraphs: In multi-agent value factorization, a mixing network combines information used to learn coordinated behavior. This paper studies what happens when increasing numbers of its neurons become inactive. Such dormant neurons reduce the network's expressive capacity, and the authors demonstrate their presence and harmful learning effects across multiple algorithms and environments.

The study also finds that dormant neurons correlate with over-active neurons, whose activation scores are large. ReBorn addresses that imbalance by transferring weights from over-active neurons to dormant ones. The intervention therefore uses activity already present in the network to reactivate capacity that is contributing little to learning.

The authors theoretically show that the weight transfer can preserve learned action preferences, so the procedure need not erase those preferences as it changes neuron activity. Experiments report promising results across environments and improvements to several popular value-factorization approaches. The work links an internal pattern of uneven neuron use to learning performance and offers a direct intervention supported by both theory and empirical evaluation.
neurips-2024-the-dormant-neuron-phenomen.tldr: ReBorn transfers weights from over-active to dormant neurons to improve multi-agent value-factorization learning while preserving learned action preferences.

paragraphs: Out-of-distribution detection asks whether an input differs from the data a classifier was trained to recognize. Existing methods often inspect class scores or the activations just before the final classifier layer. WeiPer develops a richer input representation by modifying how those activations are projected toward classes.

The method perturbs class-projection weights in the final fully connected layer. These altered projections expand the representation available for detecting unfamiliar inputs. The authors show that this modification can improve several detection methods and introduce a distance-based detector designed to use the resulting representation space.

WeiPer achieves state-of-the-art results across multiple OpenOOD benchmarks, with especially pronounced improvements when unfamiliar examples lie close to the training distribution. Those cases matter because the distinction between familiar and unfamiliar data is less clear. The paper supports its findings through theoretical motivations, empirical observations, and ablation studies, showing how a change to class projections can improve the usefulness of a pretrained classifier for detecting distribution shifts.
neurips-2024-weiper-ood-detection-using-.tldr: WeiPer perturbs a classifier's final class projections to improve detection of unfamiliar images, especially near the training distribution.
